title: ÆTHER: First Love
story: A boy sees a girl for the first time: shy glances, a skipped heartbeat, a first smile, and then the first love blooms.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 17:38: 'a romantic track of just a guy meeting a girl for the first time, then the first love.' Two halves: the meeting (mysterious, shy, minor) turns into first love (warm, major) at ~28 s. South Indian romantic film-song WRITING style (raga melody with gamakam, question-and-answer phrasing, flute/violin interlude), any instruments. Neon Raja v4 lesson: an explicit 10 s timeline naming a new lead per section gets real changes. Own sounds: heartbeat as the kick, glass bangles as the shimmer/shaker. Prompt mode (music_v2).

prompt: A brand-new romantic theme written the way the great Tamil and Telugu film composers write the BGM for the moment a boy sees a girl for the first time and falls in love. Instrumental, no lyrics. South Indian film style in the writing: a singable raga melody like Kalyani with slow gamakam slides, bends and grace notes on every lead, shy question-and-answer phrases that grow into a full love theme, a gentle swaying groove, a film-song interlude with flute and violin answering each other. About 84 BPM. A short catchy five-note love hook that returns, varied, on a NEW lead sound every 10 seconds. Our sounds: a soft heartbeat is the kick drum, glass bangles jingling are the shimmer and shaker, a glitch-chopped veena pluck is the electronic partner of the lead. Half warm real instruments, half soft modern electronic colour, never a wall of synths. Timeline: 0-8 s: mystery, only two sounds: a soft heartbeat and a breathy bamboo flute alone playing a rising three-note call (root, minor third, fifth, the last note held and bent upward), a faint bangle shimmer, they see each other. 8-18 s: a felt piano asks a shy question phrase and the glitch-chopped veena pluck answers it, stolen glances; a low warm drone. 18-28 s: the heartbeat skips one beat (the first smile), then a gentle swaying groove with hand percussion and finger snaps; the hook moves to a solo violin with slides. 28-38 s: a reversed veena swell opens into the love: the key turns from minor to bright major, lush strings and a melodic bass line enter, the hook moves to a sweet wordless female hum answered by a male hum. 38-48 s: interlude showpiece: bamboo flute and violin trade the melody phrase by phrase, faster and closer, bangles as the shaker. 48-50 s: everything holds its breath on one piano note. 50-62 s: the biggest moment: the full love melody on soaring strings and a clean electric guitar with gentle bends, wordless chorus, the hook lifted up a whole step. 62-72 s: everything falls away to the solo flute playing the three-note call again, now in major, ending on one soft bell. Not a Western pop ballad, not Hollywood, not lo-fi, not ambient, no EDM, no white-noise risers, no side-chain pumping, no long repeats of the same sound.
